History:
- Presenting complaint: acute shortness of breath for ~1 hour while sitting and watching TV.
- Onset/duration/progression: began over the last hour; patient reports associated sensation of heart "really going" (palpitations).
- Associated symptoms: cough started yesterday (non-productive, no sputum reported); chest soreness with deep breaths and tenderness around recent C-section scar.
- Context/risk factors: recent C-section 4 weeks ago; currently at home with baby who is well; no prior similar episodes reported.
- Recent medications/analgesia: codeine taken postoperatively fairly regularly but reportedly not taken for about one week.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: none reported.
- Surgical/obstetric: cesarean section 4 weeks prior (postpartum).
- Allergies: ibuprofen — reaction not documented.
- Medications: codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social/support: partner at work; patient alone at home with baby.

Physical Examination:
- General: patient alert and oriented, speaking coherently.
- Cardiorespiratory: patient reports palpitations; during teleconsult she counted 30 beats during a timed count (physician noted heart "slightly fast"); no chest pain at rest reported.
- Chest/cough: cough began yesterday, non-productive; chest and C-section scar tender, chest feels sore with deep inspiration.
- Other: baby with patient and reported to be well.
- Relevant negatives: no haemoptysis reported; no prior similar episodes reported.

Impression:
- Acute dyspnea and palpitations 4 weeks post-cesarean with recent cough — clinical concern for possible venous thromboembolism (e.g., pulmonary embolism); requires urgent hospital evaluation.

Management Plan:
- Immediate advice: proceed promptly to the hospital emergency department for further assessment.
- Transport options discussed: ambulance offered; patient elected to self-transport with baby; advised to go quickly and bring supplies for baby.
- Medication advice prior to presentation: do not take codeine before going to hospital.
- Potential treatments discussed: if a thrombus is found, hospital can provide treatment to reduce clotting (anticoagulation) — specifics to be determined by ED team.
- No tests or prescriptions initiated during teleconsult.

Patient Summary:
- Patient is a 4-week post-cesarean postpartum woman who developed acute shortness of breath and palpitations while at rest; she also has a cough that began yesterday and chest/scar tenderness. Due to concern for postpartum thromboembolism, she was advised to go to the emergency department promptly for evaluation and possible treatment.

Key Takeaways:
- Go to the hospital emergency department promptly for assessment of possible blood clot in the lungs.
- Do not take codeine before ED evaluation.
- Bring baby supplies and arrange transport; ambulance is an option if condition worsens.

Next Steps:
- Emergency department evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism/venous thromboembolism and other causes of acute dyspnea.
- ED team will determine appropriate investigations and treatments (imaging/labs and anticoagulation if indicated).
- Follow-up with primary care or obstetrics as advised by ED after evaluation.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: current vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, temperature); objective cardiopulmonary exam findings; detailed description of allergic reaction to ibuprofen; full medication list with doses and frequencies; smoking status; history of prior thromboembolism or thromboprophylaxis; details about breastfeeding status; details about leg pain/swelling.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: patient stated date of birth as "twentieth of April nineteen eighty" but physician said "nineteen eighty three" — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: audio content sufficiently clear for clinical details; some patient hesitancy and incomplete descriptions of allergy and medication dosing.
